summary: Plots a volume-weighted average price line that restarts at the first bar of each day, using the typical price by default.
overview: Session VWAP is a short example Pine script that draws one yellow line on the price chart: the volume-weighted average price for the current day. The line starts again at the first bar of every new day.
how: On each bar the script adds price times volume to a running sum, and adds volume to a second sum. The line is the first sum divided by the second. Both sums reset to zero when a new day starts.
The price used is the source setting, hlc3 by default (the average of high, low and close).
use: Some traders use VWAP as a reference for the day's average traded price.
Use it to see whether price is trading above or below the day's average.
Some traders watch how price reacts when it returns to VWAP.
Use it as an example of how Pine scripts reset values each day.
notes: It needs volume data; without volume the line is not drawn.
The day boundary follows the chart's daily session.
It has no standard-deviation bands and no alert conditions.
